newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end weaker as surging financials cool.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end weaker as surging financials cool.

text.p: Shares ended weak as surging finance and bank stocks cooled after a heady start, traders and analysts said.

The four requoted financial stocks, involved in a 2.16 billion ringgit bank merger, led volumes as punters joined the buying bandwagon. Kwong Yik Bank, Rashid Hussain, DCB and Malayan Banking all hit highs for the year before falling back in the afternoon on profit taking.
The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index fell 6.34 points to 1,220.18, after earlier hitting a year peak of 1,242.00. The Second Board index was off 15.26 to 574.78.

"Those pushing up the banking stocks are punters. Those who know the fundamentals would have sold," said Amin Manap, banking analyst at Mohaiyani Research. He said though the merger deal adds value to the counters, pushing them higher now carried a higher risk.
Most-active Kwong Yik jumped 2.20 ringgit to 9.15 on volume of 17.5 million, off its year high of 9.35. DCB rose 10 cents to 8.75, Rashid gained 90 to 16.70 and Maybank by 25 to 25.25.
Other market heavyweights were pulled down by lack of buying interest as many local fund managers took year-end holidays, traders said.
